title: His Charleston sweetheart Leotha
summary: He tells of the girl in the court who became his wife and greeted him when he returned to bury his mother.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Well then, you didn't have too, too bad, or an unhappy time then in those years at high school then?
Oh, no. No.
It was high school, then?
No, no. It was just -- no, no.
Its just the end of public school?
Right. Right.
Yeah.
Right. and uh --
You didn't play hookie? You just kept going to school and --
I went to school. I played hookie a couple of times.
Yeah. Yeah. Well, I never did ask you -- did girls or you get involved with any little girls was there a sweetheart before you left Charleston?
Yeah. Uh -- yeah.
Any little girls you were sweet on?
Yes. One A little girl. The girl that I married later on. (laugh)
(laugh) No kidding. Really?
Yeah.
How about that. Why, were you neighbors?
Huh?
Were you neighbors?
Yeah. We lived in, as I say, twelve houses in this alley,
And you all know each other?
Yeah. And my mother liked her very much. My mother was -- my mother was --
Oh, that was nice. She liked her.
She was in the church, also, you see. And my mother was, you know how mothers are.
Yeah. She thought she was the right girl for you.
Yeah. Right.
That's nice. So, she was kind of a sweetheart of yours --
Yes. Yes.
But (unintelligible), then you left.
Then I left.
Did you ever write her or anything, or --
No, not really.
No.
But, I never (laugh)--
(laugh) But you --?
But, I never forgot her (laugh).
Yeah (laugh) Yeah.
I never forgot her. I always thought about her, you know, when I -- And, when my mother died and I had to go back -- and then I think
she was about the first person that greeted me, when they found I had come, you know.
Yeah.
And she came in, and she saw me, and I saw her, and we just -- uh now grabbed her, you know, I just -- forever, you know.
Yeah. She was like home to you.
Yeah. Yeah. So, that's how we started.
-- How it started.
And then we wanted--
And then we went and got married.
Yeah.
Did you marry then? Out then?
During the same time that I was there, when I went to bury my mother.
You did. That was good. That would have pleased your mother, wouldn't it.
Yes. Yes.
So, did you not see your mother from the time you were thirteen till you were nineteen?
No. I didn't see her until -- from the time I left, I never went back.
Aw. And she never came up?
No. She stayed there.
What a shame. Well alright. We're jumping a little too far ahead.
Yeah, I know.
